notes: SHIP v1.14.404 - BLANK FORGE AISLE FIXED. This is a .401 regression and this ship closes it. TWO FUNCTIONAL LINES plus the stamp; everything else in the diff is comment. THE REPRODUCTION, confirmed by owner screenshots on the physical iPhone: tap OPEN AISLE from Build, PHANTOM navigates correctly to the FORGE 3D AISLE page, the page STAYS OPEN, the header, master metadata, close button, rack-selection strip, focus card and bottom controls all render - and the large 3D viewport is completely blank. The owner did not press the close button and the page did not close itself. Earlier close-handler theories were wrong and are abandoned. WHY THE DOM LOOKS PERFECT WHILE THE SCENE IS BLANK. The Forge HUD is STATIC MARKUP inside the sheet at :13104 - header, chips, focus card, search, close. It renders the instant .open is added, entirely independent of whether the 3D ever initialises. So a fully correct shell with a blank viewport is exactly what a stopped render loop looks like, and it is NOT evidence that the shell mounted successfully. THE MECHANISM, from the code order. forge3d_render creates the renderer at :19254, builds the scene, and calls frame() ONCE synchronously. At that instant the scene is EMPTY: the cabinets are not loaded yet. The racks arrive ASYNCHRONOUSLY at :19859, when the hero image finishes decoding, and heroImg.onload calls setLoadout, which does two very different things - it calls buildChips, which writes DOM and is therefore immediately visible, and it calls assignSlot for each of the five positions, which mutates the THREE scene and is only visible on a LATER FRAME. Nothing in this module re-renders on scene change; the animation loop is the only thing that ever paints a populated aisle. THE REGRESSION. v1.14.401 registered the aisle with RackEngine, and registration installs a per-attachment IntersectionObserver whose pause() cancels the animation frame. If that pause lands anywhere between the first frame and the hero decode, the loop is dead before the cabinets are ever drawn: the viewport keeps showing the empty first frame forever while every DOM element renders perfectly. The pause is easy to hit because forge3d_open adds .open and renders in the SAME synchronous task, so the observer is installed before the browser has laid out the newly-shown sheet. This is also exactly why the aisle passed device verify at .353 and fails now: before .401 the loop simply never stopped, so the cabinets appeared the moment the image decoded. FIX 1 - NEVER OBSERVE THE AISLE, by exclusion rather than tuning. The aisle is a FULL-SCREEN MODAL that is DISPOSED on close; it never sits hidden-but-alive, which is the only drain invariant I4 exists to stop. The observer therefore protects nothing there and can only strand it. The RACK keeps its observer, because the rack lives inside a PAGE that goes display:none while staying mounted - the real drain, and the reason I4 was written. FIX 2 - REPAINT AFTER POPULATION. setLoadout now restarts the loop through frame() if it is not running and the scene is not disposed. frame() is the correct path because it places the camera, renders, and reschedules; a bare renderer.render would draw with an unplaced camera. This makes a populated-but-invisible scene structurally impossible regardless of why a loop stopped, so the defect class cannot return through a different door. NOT DONE, deliberately: no route changed (owner barred it), no fallback added, no retry added, no special case, no fabricated data, RACK SCENE LOCK untouched, no scene internals modified. The .403 aisle trace is retained - it costs nothing, it never deployed, and it will confirm this fix on the device. GATES: 3 inline blocks compile clean x3, node --check sw.js, valid JSON, CSS braces 4557/4557 delta 0, line endings unchanged all-LF, PRECACHE untouched, three-stamp lockstep, functional diff is exactly two lines. DEVICE-VERIFY: clear the service-worker cache, open Build, tap OPEN AISLE - the aisle must DRAW its cabinets, not just its HUD. Then walk the flanks, focus a rack, close and reopen, and confirm it draws every time.
